problem: Deep RL agents are thought to learn representations over-specialized to their training task, but it was unknown whether different embodied navigation tasks actually induce different visual representations, which limits reuse of encoders for new tasks.
motivation: Reusable visual representations matter for sim-to-real transfer and for home robots that must learn new target objects over time. The paper measures task dependence with PWCCA and compares cross-task distances against same-task (random-seed) distances.
key_idea: Use PWCCA to compare visual encoders trained on disjoint object-goal sets, with same-task seed-to-seed distance as the baseline, and confirm the resulting task-agnosticism with frozen-encoder transfer experiments.
insight: Encoders trained on disjoint target-object sets (A vs B) are no farther apart in PWCCA distance than encoders trained on the same set with different seeds. Frozen encoders from A therefore transfer to B and to A∪B, and even learn B more sample-efficiently than training from scratch. Fine-tuning the policy is better still, so navigation skills transfer as well. The finding holds across SqueezeNet1.2, ResNet35, five Replica environments, and PointGoal with disjoint environment layouts. The authors suggest coverage of the visual space is an ingredient.
method: PWCCA similarity: compares layer activations of two networks over the same inputs with projection-weighted CCA (Morcos et al.), which is invariant to affine transforms and down-weights low-variance noise directions.

Task-dependence protocol: compare the A-B distance (networks trained on different tasks, averaged over N^2 pairs) against the A and B distances (same task, different seeds, N choose 2 pairs). If A-B is about equal to A/B, the representation is task-agnostic.

Task construction: the ObjectNav target objects are randomly split into disjoint, equal-sized sets A and B (3 random splits). Environment, actions and visuals stay the same; only the goals differ. Repeated on 4 more Replica scenes.

Agent: egocentric RGB plus a learnable 128-d target embedding, a visual encoder (SqueezeNet1.2 or ResNet35 with GroupNorm, ~1.7M parameters, ~80% in the encoder), a 1-layer GRU (256-d) and 2 FC layers. Trained with PPO+GAE for ~61M steps.

Transfer experiments: freeze the whole visual encoder trained on A, then learn B or A∪B either by fine-tuning the policy or by training a new policy from scratch. Sample efficiency is measured as rollouts needed to reach average reward 0.8 over 5 seeds.
Generalization checks: ResNet35 (ResNet50 shrunk to 35 layers, channels/4) and PointGoal navigation on disjoint sets of frl_apartment layouts (3 vs 3 environments).

setting.backbone: SqueezeNet1.2 and ResNet35 (GroupNorm) visual encoders + GRU policy, trained from scratch with PPO
setting.training_data: RL from scratch in Replica scenes (mainly apartment_2, plus apartment_0, office_2, room_0, frl_apartment_0), ~61M steps per policy; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (plus a GPS+Compass sensor for PointGoal)
setting.privileged: none at test time (the training reward uses GT semantic segmentation IoU)

numbers_note: No benchmark tables; results are given only as figures (PWCCA distance curves, reward/sample-efficiency curves).
results: In all settings (object-goal splits with SqueezeNet and ResNet35, 5 Replica environments, disjoint environment splits for PointGoal), A-B PWCCA distances match same-task distances, so the tasks induce no measurable difference in representation beyond the random seed. Frozen encoders from A learn B and A∪B, and reach reward 0.8 in fewer rollouts than training from scratch. Fine-tuning the policy is more efficient than a new policy.
limitations: The two tasks (disjoint object-goal sets in the same environment) are very similar, so the conclusion may not extend to more dissimilar tasks.
Results are qualitative and shown in figures only, on small Replica scenes with small networks (~1.7M parameters); PWCCA measures similarity, not usefulness for the task.
compares_to: Training from scratch (frozen vs. learned visual encoder)
